clauses.reason: The only operative command of EO 8046 is its operative paragraph, which exempts Louis A. Simon from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending May 31, 1940". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires that Louis A. Simon, who "was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 7581 of March 19, 1937, and No. 7824 of February 25, 1938", be further exempted; the order is a further exemption of an employee already exempted by earlier orders, which are separate instruments. The command is a time-limited permission for one named employee, so it ended by its own terms on May 31, 1940; that date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day), and the exclusive reading, under which it ends as that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. EO 8369 (dated March 7, 1940 in its text) recites this order by number and further exempts the same employee "for a period of one year ending May 31, 1941"; it is recorded as a later event (a separate later exemption, an extension), not as the end of this order's command, which ended by its own stated period. EO 8747 (dated April 28, 1941 in its text) recites this order by number and further exempts the same employee "for a period of six months ending November 30, 1941"; it is recorded as a later event (a separate later exemption, an extension), not as the end of this order's command, which ended by its own stated period.

research_rationale:
EO 8046 (February 11, 1939) exempts Louis A. Simon from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending May 31, 1940", under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404). I read the registered American Presidency Project transcription in full, confirmed its identity against the Common Crawl capture record (number, date, subject heading and text hash agree), and confirmed that it contains one operative command. The clause ended by its own stated period on May 31, 1940, recorded inclusive with the exclusive reading disclosed. Later extension orders are recorded as later events and do not end this order's clause. The text is a transcription (grade mirror_transcription) and the original is not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. Re-collation 2026-11-08: the working text was compared word by word with the held GPO printing (jobs/photius-gpo-volumes/output/texts/EO_8046.txt, page record in PAGE_CHECKS.csv); number, title, date, signature, completeness and every quoted span agree apart from OCR noise (printing header stamps, spaced punctuation, broken hyphens).

savings.reason: The order grants one named employee a permission to remain in service despite the retirement-age rule for a stated period and contains no savings, transition or continuing-obligation clause. Service the employee performed while the exemption was in force is a completed effect that does not depend on the order remaining in force, and no held source shows any other residual effect; it is recorded as accrued.
